notes.summary: Corrected invariant-carrier and homogeneous-test density proofs, with the genuine n-dimensional cone normalization. The supplied Wu versions contain literal domain, sign, boundary-facet, and energy-normalization defects; full-link finite dual energy does not characterize outputs.
notes.detailedSummary: For the supplied Wu21 v2 and Wu24 v1, torification is a continuous compact-link retraction onto K=X0^T and every potential factors through it. Published finite atomic model support lies in K; fixed-Reeb continuous and decreasing finite-energy limits preserve that carrier. Differences of same-ray continuous potentials form a dense real vector lattice in C(K), with an independent separation proof. Density on C(X0) is false, as demonstrated by evaluation at (1,1) versus the trivial valuation on A2. The cone has n-1 potential factors plus a radial factor, mass normalization 1/vol(xi), and energy denominator n vol(xi). Concavity gives the supporting inequality opposite to the display in Wu24 Proposition 7.3. Constant shifts contradict literal Wu21 E=S and its stated toric slice normalizer. These are source audits and partial proofs, not general existence.
notes.text:
Use only Wu21=arXiv:2106.13395v2 and Wu24=arXiv:2406.13684v1, together with elementary arguments stated here. All source references are one-based inclusive LF ranges of text.split('\n'). Full versions, hashes, literal excerpts and proof bodies are retained in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. The arguments are unverified drafts.

Let n=dim X, rho=phi_xi, K=X0^T, and V=vol(xi)=lim n! m^{-n} sum_{<xi,alpha><=m} dim R_alpha. The genuine mixed measure is V^{-1} dd phi_1 ... dd phi_{n-1} dd rho^+, with rho^+=max(rho,0), and energy is (nV)^{-1} sum_{j=0}^{n-1} integral (phi-rho)(dd phi)^j(dd rho)^{n-1-j} dd rho^+. Here dd=d'd''. Wu21 Definition 2.4, LF 205–211, and Wu24 Theorem 2.12/Definition 4.1, LF 321–332 and 522–554, specify these conventions. There are n-1 transverse factors, one radial factor, and n energy summands. The measures are probabilities, rho|X0=0, E(rho)=0, and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. A dual supremum against a finite positive measure of mass m contains the term (1-m)c; thus finite dual energy forces mass exactly one. Scaling all n factors gives MA_{a xi}(phi/a)=MA_xi(phi) and E_{a xi}(phi/a)=E_xi(phi)/a, only on one Reeb ray.

Define tau(v)(sum f_alpha)=min v(f_alpha). To verify multiplicativity, apply the action homomorphism R→R[M] and extend the valuation of Frac(R/ker v) to Laurent polynomials by the Gauss coefficient-minimum rule. Initial Laurent polynomials multiply nontrivially in the graded residue domain. Pullback gives tau(v), even with infinite evaluations. Homogeneous values are unchanged. Wu21 Lemma 2.8, LF 269–297, proves the invariant-semivaluation criterion using an invertible character matrix, so tau lands in the invariant locus and fixes it. Finite minima of continuous evaluations give continuity; homogeneous generators of the vertex ideal show that tau preserves X0. The link is compact: v(m)=0 forces all ring evaluations nonnegative, since v(g)<0 and h∈m of finite value would make v(g^r h) tend to -infinity. Nonnegative semivaluations form a closed subset of [0,infinity]^R; the finite-generator equation min v(f_j)=0 defines the closed link. The fixed locus K of tau is therefore closed and compact. Homogeneous FS formulas factor through tau; uniform limits and decreasing pointwise limits preserve that property.

Wu21 Corollary 5.7, LF 1049–1054, states finite atomic support on T-invariant points of {rho=0}. Its proof, LF 1092–1200, obtains local discreteness from tropical facets and global finiteness from compactness. The invariant current gives a finite T(k)-set. Since the divisible abelian group T(k) has no nontrivial finite quotient, every support point is invariant. Wu24 Theorem 2.12 already states the carrier X0^T. Fixed-xi continuous approximation and Theorem 6.3 decreasing-net continuity extend the carrier to finite-energy outputs: weak limits of probabilities on closed K remain on K, by testing nonnegative continuous functions vanishing there and Radon regularity. A sentence in Wu21 Proposition 5.5 says a Hessian is zero; only its determinant is forced to vanish by the Reeb direction.

Another literal defect is Wu21 Lemma 5.8, LF 1058–1091: its boundary sum uses full hyperplanes {v_i·x=0}. For psi=max(x,y), a test near (0,1) detects the x=0 term but no part of {psi=0}, disproving the printed identity. Boundary traces must use restricted oriented active facets {v_i·x=0, v_j·x<=0 for all j}, with redundancies removed. On facet interiors the active form is unique; convex finite-difference bounds imply convergence and local boundedness of gradients of smooth convex approximants. Facet intersections have lower dimension and zero facet integration measure, so exhaustion of interiors gives the restricted trace. No full-hyperplane identity or general mass coefficient is imported from that lemma.

For corrected density, let D_xi consist of restrictions to K of phi-psi with both in CPSH(a xi) for some a>0. Same-ray addition at a xi and b xi lands at ab/(a+b) xi, and scaling changes the proportional ray. Hence D_xi is a real vector space. The valid lattice identity is max(phi_1-phi_2,psi_1-psi_2)=max(phi_1+psi_2,psi_1+phi_2)-(phi_2+psi_2). Constants come from rho+c-rho. Distinct invariant points differ on some homogeneous f of positive Reeb degree d. The FS difference max{(-v(f)+A)/d,rho}-rho equals max{(A-v(f))/d,0} on K. Taking A above the finite evaluations separates the points, also when one value is infinite. The reference generators remain in this FS expression. Lattice Stone–Weierstrass proves density in C(K). Wu24 Theorem 3.5 literally states C(X0), LF 416–417, but its homogeneous separation assumption at LF 434–435 fails outside K; its printed maximum identity also needs correction. Theorem 3.6 likewise requires the torified domain.

Explicitly, on A2 with diagonal T=(G_m)^2, evaluation w at (1,1) and the generic trivial valuation v0 both lie in X0 and agree on every nonzero homogeneous monomial. But w(x-y)=infinity and v0(x-y)=0, so tau(w)=v0 and w is outside K. All genuine potential tests agree. FS potentials attain their link maximum at v0; monotonicity and constant translation give E(phi)<=phi(v0), and decreasing approximation extends this to E1. The reference test yields E^vee(delta_w)=E^vee(delta_v0)=0. Nevertheless delta_w is not an output because its carrier is wrong. The continuous test exp(-v(x-y)) separates them. This counterexample concerns the full link, not the correctly restricted target problem.

For finite-energy phi,psi the correct signs are integral(phi-psi) MA(phi) <= E(phi)-E(psi) <= integral(phi-psi) MA(psi). The continuous mixed energy terms decrease by integration by parts and Hodge; their average lies between the extreme terms. Decreasing mixed-integral continuity extends the inequalities. Wu24 Proposition 7.3 prints the first inequality reversed at LF 1247–1249. Its dual identity becomes valid after repair: E^vee(MA(phi))=E(phi)-integral phi MA(phi). The intermediate second derivative at LF 595–600 omits dd u and n-1; LF 605–610 has the correct expression (n-1)V^{-1} integral u dd u (dd phi_t)^{n-2} dd rho^+. Hodge is used only for invariant differences.

Literal Wu21 normalizers also fail a constant-shift test. For chi(f_alpha)=c<xi,alpha> on a polynomial cone, the potential is rho+c and genuine energy is c. The all-degrees truncated simplex average is S=cn/(n+1), while the equal-degree invariant is S_tilde=c. Lemma 3.16 gives this relation, but Theorem 5.15(1) prints E=S. Theorem 6.3, LF 1442–1447, prints E=((n+1)V)^{-1} integral_{P_xi} chi_tilde d lambda with lambda(P_xi)=V, giving c/(n+1). Neither printed normalization is applied. These checks do not prove an existence theorem or a complete replacement for the defective toric formula.

notes.summary: Finite dual energy has an intrinsic homogeneous FS test and every maximizing sequence is I-Cauchy with a bounded J budget. A continuous mixed-integrability estimate is repaired. These results do not realize a limit potential or identify the target as its MA.
notes.detailedSummary: On K=X0^T, the E1 dual supremum equals the homogeneous FS supremum, proved using a Radon decreasing-continuous-net argument rather than countable monotone convergence. Outputs satisfy that finite-energy test by the corrected supporting inequality. With Q_n a fixed-Reeb quasi-triangle constant, maximizing deficits Delta_j give I(phi_j,phi_k)<=n Q_n(Delta_j+Delta_k) and J_rho(phi_j)<=(n-1)Q_n(Delta_j+E^vee(mu)). Thus outputs are I^vee-Cauchy only on the known image. A repaired continuous mixed bound has explicit constant n^{n+1}/(n-1)!. No strong completeness, arbitrary weak target integration continuity, two-sided differentiation, or Euler–Lagrange equality is proved.
notes.text:
Use the carrier and corrected signs proved/audited in n1, and the fixed-Reeb I–J and quasi-triangle estimates of Wu24 Sections 4 and 6. This note is a partial proof and not a sufficient image criterion.

For a Radon probability mu on K, E^vee(mu)=sup_{phi∈E1}(E(phi)-integral phi dmu) equals the same supremum over genuine homogeneous FS functions. Here is the required net justification. If continuous f_i decrease to usc f on compact K, Radon regularity gives integral f=inf_{continuous g>=f} integral g, including -infinity by truncation. For epsilon>0 the increasing open sets {f_i<g+epsilon} cover K. Compactness and directedness give one index covering K, so inf_i integral f_i<=integral g+epsilon. Infimize over g and let epsilon tend to zero; the opposite inequality is monotonicity. Thus integrals converge along this decreasing net. Approximate any E1 potential decreasingly by FS functions and use energy continuity. This proves equality of the suprema, even if a target integral tends to -infinity. A finite supremum therefore makes every E1 potential integrable.

Consequently the condition “mu is a probability on K and sup_{FS phi}(E(phi)-integral phi dmu)<infinity” is intrinsic and necessary for an output. The corrected supporting inequality in n1 proves E^vee(MA(phi))=E(phi)-integral phi MA(phi)<infinity. This is not claimed sufficient for solvability.

A continuous mixed bound repairs Wu24 Lemma 6.4. Suppose phi_0,...,phi_{n-1} are continuous psh and nonpositive on K, B=max_i{-E(phi_i)}, and barphi=(sum phi_i)/n. Concavity gives E(barphi)>=-B. Every energy summand is nonpositive, so E(barphi)<= (1/n) integral barphi MA(barphi). Since barphi<=phi_0/n, positivity gives an upper bound (1/n^2) integral phi_0 MA(barphi). In the mixed expansion of MA(barphi), the term with one of each phi_1,...,phi_{n-1} has coefficient (n-1)!/n^{n-1}. Multiplication by the nonpositive phi_0 permits discarding all other terms for an upper bound. Hence -B<=E(barphi)<=(n-1)!/n^{n+1} integral phi_0 MA(phi_1,...,phi_{n-1}), proving the lower bound -n^{n+1}B/(n-1)!. The source's missing 1/n, omitted -E in its displayed J definition, and incorrect energy-sum endpoint cannot be used literally. This repaired bound is nonoptimal and continuous; it does not supply all general target continuity.

Let mu have finite dual energy. The FS supremum has a maximizing sequence phi_j, with Delta_j=E^vee(mu)-E(phi_j)+integral phi_j dmu→0. Write I(phi,psi)=integral(phi-psi)(MA(psi)-MA(phi)), J_psi(phi)=E(psi)-E(phi)+integral(phi-psi)MA(psi), and let Q_n satisfy I(phi,psi)<=Q_n(I(phi,theta)+I(theta,psi)). Wu24 provides I/n<=J<=((n-1)/n)I on this fixed ray.

For theta=(phi+psi)/2, the exact midpoint identity gives E(theta)-(E(phi)+E(psi))/2=(J_theta(phi)+J_theta(psi))/2 >= I(phi,psi)/(2nQ_n). Integral terms cancel. The same left side equals (Delta_mu(phi)+Delta_mu(psi))/2-Delta_mu(theta), and nonnegativity of the last deficit bounds it above by the first half-sum. Thus
I(phi_j,phi_k)<=nQ_n(Delta_j+Delta_k)→0.
Taking psi=rho, for which Delta_mu(rho)=E^vee(mu), gives
J_rho(phi_j)<=(n-1)Q_n(Delta_j+E^vee(mu)).
Wu24 Lemma 7.7 compares I with I^vee on outputs, so MA(phi_j) is I^vee-Cauchy.

This proves an intermediate potential Cauchy property without assuming variational attainment. It proves neither a genuine E1 limit nor weak convergence of the outputs to mu. Continuity of target integrals along decreasing approximations of one potential does not imply L1(mu) continuity for arbitrary weakly convergent energy-bounded potentials. A putative maximizer only yields one-sided psh variation inequalities; constrained maxima need not have zero derivatives in arbitrary directions. Therefore no Euler–Lagrange equality or intrinsic sufficient measure criterion follows from this note.

The full proofs and source checks are in P13.2-argument.md, Sections 4–5, and P13.2-paper.tex. The finite coefficient checks for n=1,...,7 in checks/check-report.json are arithmetic observations only, not exhaustive geometric results. Rerun with python3 run_checks.py.

notes.summary: A genuine irrational toric model has MA equal to a mass-one atom at a rational-rank-two quasimonomial point. A separate A2 computation explicitly disproves the reversed printed energy sign. These are restricted model computations, not general image existence.
notes.detailedSummary: For A3 with the full diagonal torus and xi=(1,sqrt2,sqrt3), the genuine FS potential max{-a1,1-a2/sqrt2,1-a3/sqrt3} has unnormalized current mass 1/sqrt6 at w=(0,sqrt2,sqrt3). The cone volume is 1/sqrt6, so its normalized MA is delta_w. The point lies on the invariant link and has rational rank two, so it is not divisorial up to real scaling. The coefficient is derived by smooth tropical Hessian integration and the coordinate determinant, with boundary mass excluded locally. For A2, MA(max{-a,s-b})=delta_(0,s) and energy is s/2; the integral against its own MA is zero and against the reference MA is s, confirming the correct supporting signs.
notes.text:
Use n1 for the genuine current convention, carrier, and energy normalization. This is a direct local model calculation within toric polynomial cones. No quotient existence theorem or defective Wu21 toric energy formula is applied.

The local coefficient can be derived under the tropical current rule used in Wu21 Corollary 5.7's proof. For L_epsilon(z)=epsilon log(1+sum exp(z_i/epsilon)) in r variables, the gradient is a diffeomorphism onto the open standard simplex. Therefore integral det(Hess L_epsilon) dz=1/r!. The superform wedge power has density r! det(Hess L_epsilon), of total mass one, and scaling shows concentration at zero as epsilon→0. The soft positive part in one variable has second derivative of integral one, also converging to an atom. Under a nonsingular linear coordinate matrix C, the superform gives two determinant factors and integration cancels one, leaving absolute determinant |det C|. This proves the local normalization instead of importing it.

First let X=A2, xi=(1,1), rho=max{-a,-b}, and phi_s=max{-a,s-b}, s>0. The homogeneous curvature line b-a=s meets the radial reference cut max{0,-a,-b} only at (0,s), and the two gradient jumps have determinant one. Near a coordinate zero, the corresponding logarithmic term can be discarded, leaving an affine function and no boundary curvature mass. Hence MA(rho)=delta_(0,0), MA(phi_s)=delta_(0,s), and V=1. The two-term energy formula gives E(phi_s)=(phi_s(0,0)+phi_s(0,s))/2=s/2. The two supporting integrals are 0 and s. In particular the reversed sign displayed in Wu24 Proposition 7.3 would assert s/2<=0, which is false.

For the irrational example take X=A3, T=(G_m)^3, xi=(1,sqrt2,sqrt3), and
rho=max{-a1,-a2/sqrt2,-a3/sqrt3},
phi=max{-a1,1-a2/sqrt2,1-a3/sqrt3}.
The potential is genuine FS: use x1,x2,x3 as homogeneous generators and shifts (0,sqrt2,sqrt3) in their numerators. The rescaled lattice-point count m^{-3}#(mQ_xi intersect Z^3) converges to Euclidean volume(Q_xi)=1/(6sqrt6), by Riemann sums since the simplex boundary has measure zero. Multiplying by 3! in the genuine volume definition gives V=1/(sqrt2 sqrt3)=1/sqrt6.

The square of the homogeneous curvature is supported on the line a2=sqrt2(a1+1), a3=sqrt3(a1+1). Outside that line at most two affine terms are active and the curvature rank is at most one, so the square vanishes. On the line rho=-a1, and the radial cut intersects it only at w=(0,sqrt2,sqrt3). Near w use t=-a1, z2=1+a1-a2/sqrt2, z3=1+a1-a3/sqrt3. The reference cut is max{0,t}; phi=-a1+max{0,z2,z3}. The common affine term has zero curvature. The coordinate matrix has absolute determinant 1/sqrt6. The smooth Hessian argument above gives
(dd phi)^2 dd rho^+=(1/sqrt6)delta_w,
so the genuine normalized MA_xi(phi)=delta_w has mass one.

At a coordinate boundary one of the three terms disappears locally, leaving curvature rank at most one; hence there is no extra boundary mass. The point w is the monomial valuation with x1 a unit and weights sqrt2,sqrt3 on x2,x3. It lies in K since min{0,sqrt2,sqrt3}=0. Its value group has rational rank two, since sqrt(2/3) is irrational. Thus it is quasimonomial on the coordinate stratum and is not a real multiple of a divisorial valuation.

This verifies that genuine irrational model outputs can already have nondivisorial support. It is a restricted toric construction and says nothing sufficient about arbitrary target measures or general normal cones. The mathematical calculation is in P13.2-argument.md, Section 6, and P13.2-paper.tex. The rational determinant samples in checks/check-report.json check arithmetic only; irrationality and the general local coefficient are argued above, not established by floating point computation.

notes.summary: Delivered preserved inputs, both proof documents, hashed literal source/proof provenance, and successful twice-compiled final TeX. Original P13.2 remains incomplete: compactness/realization, target integration, orthogonality, two-sided differentiation, and general existence are unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: The standalone paper records the partial results n1–n3 and the exact failures of attempted projective/synthetic transfers. BJ22 completeness/surjectivity uses the envelope property and target integration continuity; its smooth existence theorem cannot automatically apply to singular rational quotients. BJ23 density and measure completeness require orthogonality and do not realize Wu finite-energy potentials. Fixed-ray Cauchy estimates and bi-Lipschitzness on outputs therefore do not solve the original problem. All required files were produced; the final TeX revision compiled twice with exit code 0, 18 checks passed, and 31 LF excerpts across four matching sources were preserved. Compilation and hashes do not verify mathematics. status.json has exactly the required fields and status incomplete.
notes.text:
The unchanged original P13.2 is not solved by this deliverable. Notes n1–n3 establish/audit useful partial facts, but no intrinsic sufficient condition for all target finite-energy probabilities on X0^T and no general existence theorem is claimed. In particular there is no realization proof covering genuinely general irrational cones. Known uniqueness modulo constants on the genuine image is retained as supplied by the task; it does not imply surjectivity.

The missing passages are concrete. Wu24 decreasing closure and pointwise bounds do not prove that a product-space or I-Cauchy limit is a genuine E1 potential. BJ22 Theorem 5.11 uses the envelope property for normalized compactness; Theorem 12.8 uses that property and Proposition 9.19 for surjectivity/completeness. Proposition 9.19's target integration continuity relies on uniform approximation by model-MA measures. Theorem 8.5 obtains two-sided extended-energy differentiation through projective relative volumes, added polarizations and fixed mixed masses; Theorem 9.11 and Corollary 9.12 then identify maximizing output limits and give Euler–Lagrange equality. Those cone analogues are not proved here. BJ23 Definition 2.15 and Proposition 2.19 require an actual orthogonality limit; Theorems 2.23 and 2.26 give measure density/completeness under that hypothesis, not realization as Wu E1 potentials. A rational quotient may be singular, whereas the supplied BJ22 Theorem 12.9 assumes smoothness; preserving the torus-invariant carrier and potential class also needs proof. Individual rational-Reeb approximation and proportional addition do not give the required uniform estimates for two changing nonproportional polarizations. No conditional template, attainment hypothesis, inverse-potential restatement, or closure of unknown outputs is offered as a characterization.

Artifacts are P13.2-argument.md (full partial argument), P13.2-paper.tex (standalone paper), and P13.2-paper.pdf (final revision: 9 pages, 338487 bytes). input.json is unchanged; input-original.json is byte-identical with SHA-256 ebad4ee6286020bd9bed2a674406481056d0dc309903336cf3aa49049f988ae1. assignment-original.txt retains the exact decoded assignment and task-original.json the unchanged task object. status.json has exactly id,status,exact_result,proof_file,concrete_gaps; its status is incomplete and the six unresolved passages are explicit.
